As China’s lunar New Year approached, there was not much activity in the imported cathode spot market. Last week, spot premium quotations for imported cathode remained flat and fell slightly going into this week, as the SHFE/LME cash month price ratio contracted. Traders reported that the quotations for imported cathode were in the US$110-130/t range last week. This week, the high end quotation declined to $120/t, whereas spot premium quotations for SXEW were quoted between US$100/t and $110/t. However, we heard that very few or almost © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **January 2012** www.crugroup.com no deals were closed as most consumers continued to exhibit more cautious buying behaviour amid subdued cathode demand. According to preliminary data from Chinese customs, China’s unwrought copper and copper semis imports surged to 508,940t in December which is a record high and up 56,920t m-o-m. We understand that the increase was driven by improved arbitrage and financing opportunities. The latter was the most important factor as indicated by the weak end-use cathode demand at the end of 2011. At the same time we noticed that cathode inventories in SHFE and Shanghai bonded warehouses both increased from December. SHFE inventories rose by 28,014t in December m-o-m and have risen by 38,426t as of 20th January compared to the end of 2011. We were told by market participants that cathode inventories in Shanghai bonded warehouses were between 300,000t-320,000t at the time of writing and may continue to increase during the week-long lunar New Year break. # **China’s non-ferrous metals industry 12****th** **five year plan** China’s non-ferrous metals industry 12th five year plan, which will guide non-ferrous metals industry development, was announced by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently. According to the plan, China’s nonferrous metals demand is expected to continue to increase but the growth rate will slow down. Refined copper consumption was 7.53Mt in 2010 with average growth of 15% from 2005 to 2010 and is forecast to be 9.7Mt in 2015 with an average growth rate of 5.2% from 2011 to 2015. Refined copper output is expected to be 6.5Mt in 2015, given average annual growth of 7.3% from 2011 to 2015. The plan proposes a reduction in the fuel consumption of copper smel

ting from 399kg standard coal/t in 2010 to 300kg standard coal/t in 2015. The output of the top ten refined copper producers is expected to account for 90% of total domestic output in 2015 compared to 76% in 2010. In terms of copper semis fabrication, the development of high quality copper alloy products and copper clad aluminium products will be encouraged. Copper mine capacity on a contained copper basis is forecast to increase to 1.3Mt/y by 2015 through exploration of domestic and over-seas copper deposits. Secondary refined copper production is expected to account for 40% of total refined copper production in 2015 compared to 38% in 2010. We are inclined to believe that some targets mentioned in the plan, e.g. the production and consumption goals in 2015, are conservative, while others, e.g. reduction in fuel required and centralization rate, are a little overestimated Nonetheless, we believe that the general development trend for the copper industry set out in the 12th five year plan is more important than the specific figures. We will discuss this plan in more detail in the next fortnightly report. # **State Grid power grid investment plan in 2012** It was reported that State Grid’s power grid investment in 2011 amounted to RMB301.9B and according to its power grid investment plan, a further RMB309.7B are expected to be invested in 2012. However, we have noticed that the investment plan and final completed investments © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 4 **January 2012** www.crugroup.com can differ. According to historical State Grid’s power grid investment figures, the y-o-y growth rate is expected to be 5.9% in 2012 and 10.6% in 2011. In 2012, State Grid will start construction of 69,000km of 110kV and above AC line and 6,146km of DC line. It will put into operation 57,000km of 110 kV and above AC line and 2,095km of DC line. Electricity sales are expected to be 3.37 trillion kWh, up 9% y-o-y. We believe that these substantial power investments will continue to boost wire and cable demand. However, some market insiders are worried about a slowdown in investments. In addition, they expect the State Grid investment to be mainly on inter-regional electricity transmission and transformation. Copper wire and cable is mainly used in the urban power grid, property development and manufacturing expansions. Therefore, the impact on copper demand may be minimal. # **Copper price rally** SHFE 3-month price

The LME 3-month copper prices r

ose to over $8,400/t this week, driven by positive economic indicators from China and a decline in LME cathode inventories.  Similarly, the SHFE 3-month copper price rallied to above RMB60,000/t.  We noticed that the Shanghai physical discount widened to around RMB500/t in the run up to the lunar New Year break as weak demand and a high copper price constrained buying interest.  According to the latest SHFE report, cathode inventories were 131,645t on 20<sup>th</sup> January up 26,387t compared to two weeks ago. Most 

consumers are very cautious to purchase raw materials, fearing copper price volatility during the New Year break.  Based on NBS data, China’s GDP growth rate in 2011 was 9.2%.  The continuous decline in the quarterly GDP growth rate and lower inflation during 2011 is expected to motivate the government to ease monetary policy with the aim of supporting economic growth in 2012.  The SHFE market will be closed next week. We expect that the SHFE 3-month copper price will catch up with the LME copper price movements when the SHFE re-opens the week after next.
